title: Seamless Plan Migration: Credit Preservation and Dual-Billing Reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Enable customers to migrate between legacy and new plan types without losing prepaid credits, with deterministic quota normalization and an auditable dual-billing reconciliation window. This PRD defines the functional requirements, non-functional constraints, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and edge-case handling for the migration flow. Background: We will be launching a redesigned plan taxonomy (compute+call entitlements) and a new billing engine. Some customers must be migrated automatically; others will self-serve. The migration must preserve monetary value (credits), maintain per-route and per-model rate limits, avoid double-charging, and supply clear invoice line-items when both billing systems overlap during the transition window.
requirements: Preserve remaining monetary credit when a customer migrates from legacy plan A to new plan B; credit should convert at a deterministic exchange that is stored in ledger and visible in console.

Map legacy quota units (tokens/embedding-requests/calls) to the new hybrid entitlement model (compute credits + call-units) with documented conversion tables and per-customer override when conversion causes >10% delta in usable capacity.

Support a configurable reconciliation window (default 72 hours) where the legacy billing engine can still ingest usage while the new engine starts accepting new events; during this window we must prevent duplicate charges via request-level idempotency keys and reconciliation markers.
Expose migration preview in Console showing: projected charges for remainder of billing cycle under new plan, preserved credit amount, rate-limit changes, and any manual approvals required.

When a customer-initiated rollback occurs within the reconciliation window, the system must revert quota mappings and reapply preserved credits; invoices generated during the window must be flagged as provisional until reconciliation completes.

All conversions and reconciliations must be auditable: store original usage rows, converted units, exchange rates used, responsible actor (automated/system/PMT/customer), and a reconciliation status field.

Provide a migration API endpoint for programmatic migrations with idempotency, dry-run mode, and a request schema that includes 'preserve_credits': true|false and 'accept_quota_delta_threshold': percentage.
Notify customers via email and in-console messages at three points: 7 days before migration, immediately after migration, and when reconciliation completes or if manual intervention required.
Allow billing Ops to run manual reconciliation jobs with per-customer dry-run preview and an expunge mode to archive legacy usage rows after reconciliation approval.

Rate-limit mapping: legacy per-caller concurrency and per-route burst credits must be translated into new per-caller priority shares; provide fallback rules for incompatible mappings (e.g., split into soft limits + graceband).
non_functional_requirements: Reconciliation correctness >= 99.995% (measured as percentage of usage rows reconciled without manual resolution) for first 30 days after rollout.
Migration preview must render in < 3s for customers with <= 100 active routes; for enterprise customers with >1000 routes, background generation with email when done is acceptable.
All migration and reconciliation actions must be logged with WORM (write-once) audit retention of 540 days.
System must support simultaneous migrations across regions; cross-region conversion rates must be consistent and recorded (no per-region arbitrary rounding differences).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Credit preservation - for 10 sampled accounts (including trial, prepaid, and committed), migrating preserves monetary value within +/- $0.50 after conversion and appears on migration-preview and final invoice.

AC-2: No double-charge - simulate concurrent events against legacy and new billing engines during the 72-hour window; no account should have duplicate invoice line items for the same usage_id when using idempotency keys.

AC-3: Quota mapping parity - for 5 representative workloads per customer (chat, embeddings, rerank, high-throughput batch), post-migration effective throughput must be within 10% of pre-migration capacity or a mitigation path (manual override) is presented.

AC-4: Auditability - all migrated accounts show a complete conversion audit trail in Console and the audit export contains: original usage_row_id, converted_units, exchange_rate, migration_job_id, actor, and timestamp.
AC-5: Reconciliation automation - reconciliation job re-maps >99% of overlapping usage rows automatically; remaining rows surface in Ops dashboard with clear root-cause tags.

AC-6: Rollback correctness - trigger customer-initiated rollback within window for 3 test accounts; post-rollback invoice state and quotas match pre-migration values and provisional invoices are canceled/updated accordingly.
AC-7: Notifications - customers with migration scheduled receive the three required notifications; sampled customer confirms message content and timing.
AC-8: API behavior - migration API returns idempotent 2xx for repeated calls with same idempotency key and has working dry-run mode that shows projected delta without changing ledger state.
AC-9: Performance - generating migration-preview for a mid-sized customer (250 routes) completes within 10s; otherwise returns 202+poll endpoint.
AC-10: Security - all sensitive fields in migration payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest; security review signoff recorded.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Migrate 5 low-risk sandbox orgs and 3 internal Redwood tenants. Run automated reconciliation and validate ACs over 7 days.
Phase 1 (beta opt-in): Open migration to 50 customers who opt-in via Console; provide account manager support and run daily manual reconciliation checks.
Phase 2 (automated migration): Start automated migrations for small customers (< $500/mo) in waves of 200/day; monitor reconciliation-error-rate, invoices reconciled, and customer tickets.
Phase 3 (enterprise coordination): Coordinate with Sales and Solutions for enterprise migrations; require signed migration acknowledgement and schedule a dedicated migration window per customer.

Rollback strategy: Keep legacy billing engine writable for reconciliation window (default 72h). If errors > threshold, pause automated migrations and revert remaining scheduled jobs. Provide per-account rollback button in Ops UI.
Communication: publish migration runbook for Support and CSM teams; create a Console banner for migrated customers linking to migration-details page and invoice glossary.
open_questions: Q1: Conversion formula governance - who signs off on exchange rates for prepaid credits (Finance, PM, or Legal)?
Q2: Graceband for quota delta - should we offer automatic top-up credits when conversion reduces usable capacity > 15% for enterprise accounts?
Q3: Tax handling - how are taxes applied when credit conversion triggers invoice adjustments mid-cycle?
Q4: External integrations - do any downstream ERP systems expect legacy invoice line-item ids that will be changed after reconciliation?
Q5: Default reconciliation window - is 72 hours acceptable for all regions or should we allow per-customer configuration?
decisions: D1: Use 72-hour default reconciliation window but make it configurable per-customer via Ops (approved 2026-02-18).
D2: Preserve monetary value by converting remaining credits to a unified 'compute-credit' unit with Finance-provided exchange table; record both original and converted amounts in ledger.
D3: Migration API will require idempotency_key and support dry-run mode; success response includes migration_job_id and reconciliation_estimate.
D4: For quota deltas > 10% and < 25% present customer-facing mitigation choices; >25% require manual Sales/CS approval before automated migration.
test_cases: TC-01: Single-user migration dry-run: call migration API dry-run, verify no ledger change and preview accuracy.
TC-02: Concurrent-event simulation: send duplicate events to legacy and new engines with same usage_id and confirm only one billed row accepted.
TC-03: Large-route customer: run migration-preview for customer with 2k routes; ensure fallback to async generation and email notification when complete.
TC-04: Edge-case negative balance: migrate account with -$12.34 balance and verify preserved credit behavior and invoice adjustments.
TC-05: Rollback flow: trigger rollback for test customer and verify quotas and invoices restored.
